short: A slow infantry tank that could climb ground no other armour could reach.
full:
The A22 was specified in 1940 in the expectation that fighting would return to the conditions of 1918, which is why it has long tracks running the full height of the hull and eleven forward gears. It entered service in June 1941 with a hastily developed Bedford engine and a reputation for breaking down. Its combat debut, at Dieppe on 19 August 1942, was a failure: most of the tanks landed bogged on the shingle and none got clear of the town.

Tunisia and Italy showed what it was actually for. Heavily armoured and geared for torque rather than speed, it climbed slopes that were assumed to be impassable to tanks, at Longstop Hill and again at Monte Camino. The hull became the basis for the specialised vehicles of 79th Armoured Division: the AVRE with its petard demolition mortar, the Crocodile flamethrower and the ARK bridging tank. Around 7,300 were built, and the Churchill left British service in 1952 after a final campaign in Korea.
